title: The Harmful Effects Of Glyphosate, The Most Common Agrochemical
summary: Podcast with a litigator arguing glyphosate (Roundup) is a carcinogen and gut toxin sprayed on much of the food supply, approved by captured regulators.

assertions.quote: glyphosate or weed killer called Roundup which is on 70 percent of our food and has been linked to cancer and microbiome issues

verdicts.note: EPA's 2017 assessment found no dietary or drinking-water risks of concern from glyphosate residues, including for infants, children and pregnant women; a regulator's own finding whose human-health decision was vacated in 2022 and is being redone in late 2026.

EFSA's 2023 peer review put the maximum chronic dietary intake of glyphosate at 3% of the ADI (Dutch toddlers) and acute intake at 2% of the ARfD; provisional, limited to the EU's representative uses, but an independent regulator finding dietary residues far below levels of concern.
CDC's NHANES biomonitoring finds glyphosate in most Americans' urine but states that detection does not mean it causes disease and that other studies must determine which levels are safe.

assertions.quote: there's a good chance one or more of his ingredients was doused in Roundup or weed killer before it left the farm

verdicts.note: Residue testing finds glyphosate commonly in grain, oat and soy foods, usually far below tolerances, but rarely on most fresh produce.
EPA confirms low levels of glyphosate are found in common food products because of its widespread use, while FDA testing has found none above tolerances; no prevalence figure is given.

assertions.quote: they began telling Farmers spray this on the crop on your wheat right before Harvest

verdicts.note: Pre-harvest desiccation with glyphosate is a registered, documented practice on wheat, oats and pulses, though used on a minority of US wheat acres.

assertions.quote: 2006 marks that day when suddenly these gluten allergies began exploding and the Celiac

verdicts.note: Celiac disease is a genetic autoimmune condition; the glyphosate link rests on an ecological time-trend correlation, and rising celiac rates predate 2006.

assertions.quote: people understand that glyphosate is toxic to the microbiome

verdicts.note: Glyphosate inhibits a pathway some gut bacteria use and shifts microbiota in some animal studies, but effects at human dietary doses are not established.

EFSA reviewed the published gut-microbiome studies and found no definitive conclusions can be drawn from them, while judging the mammalian toxicity dataset protective for any microbiome-mediated effect.

assertions.quote: that's a probable carcinogen and that happened in 2015. for glyphosate

verdicts.note: IARC rates glyphosate a probable carcinogen and some meta-analyses find a modest lymphoma association at the highest exposures, but the large Agricultural Health Study found none.

IARC's pooled analysis of the case-control studies plus the Agricultural Health Study gave a statistically significant NHL association, but the large AHS cohort alone found none and IARC rates the human evidence only 'limited'.

EPA concluded glyphosate is not likely to be carcinogenic under real-world exposures, in line with EFSA, ECHA, Canada, Australia, Japan and JMPR, while noting IARC's hazard-based 2A rating answers a different question.

EFSA concluded the available human epidemiological studies do not provide conclusive evidence that glyphosate exposure is associated with any cancer-related effect, and ECHA rated it unlikely to be carcinogenic; it does not single out heavily exposed groups.

In the prospective Agricultural Health Study of 54,251 licensed applicators (44,932 glyphosate users), the top quartile of intensity-weighted lifetime use had no raised NHL risk (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.64-1.20, 440 exposed cases), with no association for any subtype; exposure was self-reported, so some misclassification is expected.

A meta-analysis of the highest exposure groups in the 2018 AHS cohort and five case-control studies found a 41% raised NHL risk (meta-RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.13-1.75); five of the six studies are case-control.

A 2026 meta-analysis of ten datasets found the highest-exposure NHL estimate was not significant with all studies included (random-effects OR 1.18, 95% CI 0.97-1.44), and became significant (OR 1.33-1.47) only after dropping the two cohort studies, so the raised risk rests on the case-control evidence.

Pooling three farmer cohorts (316,270 farmers in France, Norway and the USA), ever use of glyphosate was not associated with NHL overall but was with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (meta-HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.00-1.85); it measures ever versus never use, not heavy use.

assertions.quote: you can grow as much food or more food better food without all those chemicals

verdicts.note: AAP clinical report (abstract only) says well-designed farming studies show yields comparable to conventional farming.
The review notes generally lower crop yields in organic systems, typically limited by nitrogen availability; cited in passing, not analysed.

Hierarchical meta-analysis of 115 studies (1071 comparisons, 38 countries) found organic yields 19.2% lower (95% CI 15.5-22.9%), with conventional higher for all crop types; the authors note publication bias may overstate the gap.

assertions.quote: it destroys this oil biome and because of that it makes the soil kind of impervious

verdicts.note: Studies show some effects on soil microbes, fungi and earthworms, but many field studies find small or transient effects at label rates.

EPA reads the literature as mixed, with effects on soil microbes not consistently shown and often from unrealistically high doses, and expects no long-term effect because glyphosate does not persist in soil; it also enables no-till, which spares soil life from tillage.

assertions.quote: it was EPA acting as a sock puppet for the industry that it was supposed to regulate

verdicts.note: Litigation documents show industry influence on some reviews, but several independent agencies worldwide also judged dietary glyphosate unlikely to pose a cancer risk.

Many separate regulators (EFSA, ECHA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, FAO/WHO JMPR) reached EPA's conclusion, and EPA attributes the IARC split to hazard versus real-world risk scope; IARC (L219-221) notes regulators lean on unpublished industry data, which differs from capture.
